slides.0.title: Other BC Regions
slides.0.subtitle: Similkameen, Fraser Valley, Vancouver Island, the Gulf Islands and Thompson-Shuswap
slides.1.title: Similkameen Valley
slides.1.highlights.0.title: A dry valley
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A narrow east–west corridor along the Similkameen River, about 27 km between Hedley and Cawston; semi-arid with about 330 mm of rain a year, summer highs of 30–35°C and diurnal swings that sometimes exceed 20°C (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Organic capital
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Similkameen holds a disproportionate share of BC's certified organic vineyards and is called Canada's organic capital; it has no sub-GIs (Wine With Seth). Acreage and winery counts differ slightly by source (about 700 or 768 acres; 20-plus or 22 wineries) and are not tested
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Grapes
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Syrah stands out among warm-climate reds, Bordeaux varieties (Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot) anchor red blends and Pinot Noir grows on cooler upper slopes; whites include Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Riesling and Gewürztraminer. Whether Cabernet Sauvignon or Syrah leads varies by page (Wine With Seth, GuildSomm)
slides.1.content: Similkameen is dry, windy in places and strongly organic.
slides.2.title: Coast and islands: a cool maritime climate
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Fraser Valley
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A cool, wet maritime climate suited to aromatic whites and cool-climate reds such as Pinot Noir; about 43 wineries and 194 acres (GuildSomm, single source)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vancouver Island and Cowichan Valley
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A cool coastal maritime climate where Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Ortega are key; about 22 wineries and 321 acres (GuildSomm). Cowichan Valley was recognised as a sub-GI on 10 July 2020, the first outside the Okanagan; common varieties are Ortega, Bacchus, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris, Maréchal Foch and Pinot Noir (Wine Industry Advisor)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Gulf Islands
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A maritime microclimate with mild winters; Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris make up 53% of vines; about 12 wineries and 110 acres (GuildSomm)
slides.2.content: Coastal and island wines are shaped by a cool maritime climate.
slides.3.title: Small inland regions
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Thompson Valley and Lillooet
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Thompson Valley has a continental climate with hot summers and cold winters and grows Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Marquette and Maréchal Foch, with about 3 wineries and 93 acres; Lillooet has hot days and cool nights suited to Syrah, Merlot and Sauvignon Blanc, with about 2 wineries and 50 acres, the smallest GI (GuildSomm)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Shuswap
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Lake-influenced, with warm summers and cool, wet winters; Siegerrebe and Ortega together make up 24% of vines and Maréchal Foch is the most planted red (21%); about 9 wineries and 107 acres (GuildSomm, single source)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Kootenays
slides.3.highlights.2.content: High-altitude vineyards (450–750 m) with a cool continental climate; Pinot Noir 27% and Gewürztraminer 9%; about 6 wineries and 116 acres (GuildSomm, single source)
slides.3.content: The inland regions are small, each with its own signature grapes.
